definitions.multiSymbol: |S(T)| > 1 where S(T) = declarations whose name is T, plus declarations whose qualifiedName is exactly T, deduped on (file, qualifiedName, kind, startLine)
definitions.multiKind: |{kind : d in S(T)}| > 1 — this is script/m14/incoming-check.ts's rule, reproduced verbatim
definitions.B1_lineSettled: the edge's OWN file declares T, and a visibility rule names exactly one declaration (unique, or picksOne). THE EDGE IS TRUE; resolving by bare name is what is weak.
definitions.B2b_fileAbsent: the edge's own file declares T ZERO times. The collision is entirely in other files, so the declaration this edge names is reachable only through a module path, which the published bare name does not carry.
definitions.B2c_noneVisible: the edge's own file declares T more than once and no candidate satisfies the ORDER rule at the edge's line — the edge precedes every local declaration of that name.
definitions.B3_indistinct: several candidates satisfy the ORDER rule at the edge's line and the last-declared tie-break cannot separate them — same startLine, same name, one file. The published NAME cannot express this.
definitions.precedence: over the multiSymbol population: B3 and B2c and B1 and B2b partition it, because B2b is decided first (own-file candidate count) and the rest by the ORDER verdict
definitions.visibilityOrderRule: candidate declared at or before the edge's line (startLine <= l); among those the LAST wins, because a later local of the same name shadows an earlier one from its own declaration onward. THIS IS THE CORRECT RULE FOR LUA: a local at line 10 is visible at line 20.
definitions.visibilitySpanRule: candidate's own span covers the line (startLine <= l <= endLine); innermost (shortest span) wins. RETAINED ONLY to measure the instrument's own sensitivity — a forward reference is invisible to it.
definitions.visibilityRuleSensitive: edges where the ORDER verdict and the SPAN verdict disagree. This is how much the rule choice moves the buckets.
definitions.stdlibListIs: TRANSCRIBED from the Lua 5.4 reference manual, NOT derived from the corpus — the claim is 'named in the documented stdlib surface'
